review.scope: Four rates 44.1/48/96/192 kHz; 1/2/6 channels; orders 2/4/8; DF-I/TDF-II; legacy/ordered Stereo; 2x/4x; cold/warm. Each source stream has identical absolute-sample automation and is rendered in single-frame versus 17/257/1024-frame partitions.
review.positive_controls: All 288 warmed static-filter renders are bit-identical before automation; static equality is asserted separately.
review.other_invariants: Every measured valid scalar setter and process callback has zero allocations/deallocations; outputs are finite. All matrix cases complete before equality assertion fails.
review.diagnosis: Oversampler buffers 256 source frames and invokes EQ on a complete internal chunk. EQ advances transition time by public source callbacks and reconciles internal frame counts after processing, so the coefficient trajectory applied to a chunk depends on the callback that completes it. Interrupted edits can supersede controls for buffered source audio.
review.next_requirement: Retain a bounded, source-timestamped control trajectory across oversampler buffering and apply it on the internal audio timeline; verify independent timing, interruption, lifecycle and RT behavior. A callback partition convention or looser tolerance is not an accepted fix.
limits: No production scheduling fix in this checkpoint.
This is audio partition equivalence, not an independent oversampled transfer oracle.
No CPU deadline or arbitrary filter-family claim.
Earlier five-millisecond tests check state retirement, not full rendered waveform equivalence.
review.initial_provenance: Initial result came from a temporary extension of audit_transitions.rs, moved into the opt-in QA example without weakening equality. The native regression remains unchanged and no new ignored test was introduced.
